description: People, places and peoples named in the translated text, for the reader's cards. Keyed by Strong's number (G or H) and the lemma, which is copied from MACULA. A name used of more than one person has one sense per referent: a sense with "verses" applies to those verse ids, a sense without them to every other verse. Notes are English, written from what the passages say and widely agreed history and geography; every entry is an AI draft until a named reviewer approves it.

senses.name: the Jews
senses.note: The Jewish people, descendants of Israel who keep the law of Moses. In John the word often means the religious authorities in Jerusalem who oppose Jesus, and sometimes Judeans or Jewish crowds generally; Paul pairs Jew and Greek to cover all humanity.

senses.name: Moses
senses.note: The Israelite leader who brought Israel out of Egypt and through whom God gave the law at Sinai. In these passages he stands for the law itself, and his writings are said to point to Jesus.

senses.name: Jerusalem
senses.note: The chief city of Judea and site of the temple, where Jews went up for the great festivals. Much of Jesus' ministry in John takes place there during the feasts.

senses.name: Martha
senses.note: Sister of Mary and Lazarus in Bethany near Jerusalem, a family Jesus loved. When Lazarus died she met Jesus on the road and spoke with him about the resurrection.

senses.name: Philip
senses.note: One of the twelve disciples, from Bethsaida, the hometown of Andrew and Peter. Jesus called him directly; he brought Nathanael to Jesus and was tested by Jesus before the feeding of the crowd.

senses.name: Seth
senses.note: The third son of Adam and Eve, born after Abel was killed, and father of Enosh. Genesis 5 traces the line from Adam to Noah through him.

senses.name: Eden
senses.note: The region where God planted the garden in which he placed the first man, with a river flowing out of it. The man was later sent out of the garden. Its location is unknown.

senses.name: Nathanael
senses.note: A man from Cana in Galilee whom Philip brought to Jesus. At first doubtful about Nazareth, he declared Jesus Son of God and King of Israel. He is often thought to be the Bartholomew of the other Gospels, but this is uncertain.

senses.name: Kenan
senses.note: Son of Enosh and father of Mahalalel in the line from Adam to Noah in Genesis 5; he is said to have lived 910 years.

senses.name: Babylon
senses.note: The capital of the Babylonian empire on the Euphrates, to which the people of Judah were deported in the sixth century BC; Matthew uses the deportation to divide Jesus' genealogy.

senses.name: Babylon (where Peter writes from)
senses.note: The place Peter sends greetings from at the close of his letter. It is probably a figurative name for Rome, the imperial capital, though some take it literally.

senses.name: the Samaritans
senses.note: The people of Samaria, between Judea and Galilee, who worshipped the God of Israel but centred their worship on Mount Gerizim and accepted only the books of Moses. Jews and Samaritans were long hostile to one another.

senses.name: Bethany beyond the Jordan
senses.note: The place on the east side of the Jordan where John was baptizing. It is distinct from Bethany near Jerusalem, and its location is uncertain.

senses.name: Bethany
senses.note: A village on the Mount of Olives about two miles from Jerusalem, home of Martha, Mary and Lazarus, whom Jesus raised from the dead.

senses.name: Solomon
senses.note: Son of David and Bathsheba and king of Israel after him, famed for his wisdom and for building the first temple. He appears in Jesus' genealogy, and a colonnade of the temple courts bore his name.

senses.name: Isaac
senses.note: Son of Abraham and Sarah, husband of Rebecca and father of Jacob and Esau. He is the son through whom God's promise to Abraham was to continue.

senses.name: Noah
senses.note: Son of Lamech and father of Shem, Ham and Japheth. His father named him in hope of relief from the toil caused by the cursed ground; he is later the one saved through the flood.

senses.name: Mark
senses.note: John Mark, cousin of Barnabas, who travelled with Paul and was later with him in his imprisonment. Peter calls him his son, probably meaning spiritual son; early tradition links him with the Gospel of Mark.

senses.name: Tychicus
senses.note: A trusted co-worker of Paul from the province of Asia, who carried Paul's letters to Colossae and Ephesus and brought news of him to the churches.

senses.name: Ram
senses.note: Son of Hezron and father of Amminadab, an ancestor of David in the line of Judah listed in Jesus' genealogy. Nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Hezekiah
senses.note: King of Judah around 715 to 686 BC, son of Ahaz and father of Manasseh, remembered as a faithful reformer. He is listed among the kings in Jesus' genealogy.

senses.name: Azor
senses.note: An ancestor of Jesus after the exile, son of Eliakim and father of Zadok in Matthew's genealogy. Nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Macedonia
senses.note: The Roman province in northern Greece, including Philippi and Thessalonica. Paul founded churches there, and they gave generously to the poor believers in Jerusalem.

senses.name: Pontus
senses.note: A Roman region on the southern coast of the Black Sea in northern Asia Minor (modern Turkey), one of the areas where the believers Peter writes to were living.

senses.name: Christian
senses.note: A name for followers of Christ, first used in Antioch and probably given by outsiders. Peter tells believers not to be ashamed to suffer under this name.

senses.name: Balaam
senses.note: A prophet, son of Beor, hired by the king of Moab to curse Israel in the time of Moses. Peter uses him as an example of a teacher who loved the reward of wrongdoing.

senses.name: Onesimus
senses.note: A believer from Colossae, sent with Tychicus to bring news of Paul. He is probably the runaway slave on whose behalf Paul wrote to Philemon.

senses.name: Hierapolis
senses.note: A city in the Lycus valley of Asia Minor, near Laodicea and Colossae, where Epaphras also worked for the believers.

senses.name: Laodicea
senses.note: A wealthy city in the Lycus valley of Asia Minor, about ten miles from Colossae. Paul asks that letters be exchanged between the churches there; the letter from Laodicea is not known to survive.

senses.name: Cephas
senses.note: The Aramaic name, meaning rock, that Jesus gave to Simon son of John; Peter is its Greek equivalent.

senses.name: the Romans
senses.note: The people of Rome, whose empire ruled Judea in Jesus' time. The council feared that Rome would take away their temple and nation if Jesus' following grew.

senses.name: Salim
senses.note: A place near Aenon, where John baptized because there was plenty of water. The location is uncertain; it may have been in the Jordan valley or in Samaria.

senses.name: Bethesda
senses.note: A pool in Jerusalem near the Sheep Gate, surrounded by five porticoes, where Jesus healed a man who had been ill for thirty-eight years. Remains of a double pool have been found north of the temple area. Manuscripts vary on the name.

senses.name: Perez
senses.note: Son of Judah and Tamar, twin brother of Zerah, and an ancestor of David listed in Jesus' genealogy.

senses.name: Amminadab
senses.note: Son of Ram and father of Nahshon, an ancestor of David in the tribe of Judah listed in Jesus' genealogy.

senses.name: Obed
senses.note: Son of Boaz and Ruth and father of Jesse, so the grandfather of King David. He is listed in Jesus' genealogy.

senses.name: Abijah
senses.note: Son of Rehoboam and king of Judah for about three years, listed among the kings in Jesus' genealogy.

senses.name: Ahaz
senses.note: King of Judah in the eighth century BC, son of Jotham and father of Hezekiah, remembered for unfaithfulness. He is listed among the kings in Jesus' genealogy.

senses.name: Abiud
senses.note: Son of Zerubbabel and father of Eliakim in Matthew's genealogy of Jesus. Nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Eleazar
senses.note: Son of Eliud and father of Matthan, the great-grandfather of Joseph in Matthew's genealogy of Jesus. Nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Hebrews
senses.note: A name for the Israelite people. By calling himself a Hebrew born of Hebrews, Paul stresses his pure Jewish descent and probably his use of the ancestral language.

senses.name: the Philippians
senses.note: The believers in Philippi, a Roman colony in Macedonia where Paul founded a church. They supported his work financially from the start.

senses.name: Illyricum
senses.note: A Roman province on the eastern shore of the Adriatic Sea, roughly the western Balkans. Paul names it as the limit of his preaching from Jerusalem.

senses.name: Prisca
senses.note: A Jewish believer, also called Priscilla, wife of Aquila and co-worker with Paul. The couple risked their lives for him and hosted a church in their home.

senses.name: Junia
senses.note: A Jewish believer, probably a woman and possibly Andronicus's wife, who had been in prison with Paul and became a believer before him; Paul calls the pair prominent among the apostles.

senses.name: Apelles
senses.note: A believer in Rome whom Paul greets as tested and found true in Christ; nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Tryphaena
senses.note: A woman in the church in Rome, greeted with Tryphosa (perhaps her sister) as a hard worker in the Lord; nothing more is known of her.

senses.name: Asyncritus
senses.note: A believer in Rome whom Paul greets with others and the believers with them; nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Hermas
senses.note: A believer in Rome whom Paul greets; nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Olympas
senses.note: A believer in Rome whom Paul greets along with Philologus, Julia and others; nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Sosipater
senses.note: A Jewish believer with Paul when he wrote to the Romans, who sends greetings. He may be Sopater of Berea, who travelled with Paul, but this is uncertain.

senses.name: Quartus
senses.note: A believer with Paul in Corinth who sends greetings to Rome; Paul calls him a brother. Nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Hosea
senses.note: An Israelite prophet of the eighth century BC. Paul quotes his book to show that God calls people who were not his people to be his own.

senses.name: Cush
senses.note: A land around which the river Gihon is said to wind. Elsewhere Cush is the region south of Egypt (ancient Nubia), but its meaning here is uncertain.

senses.name: Nod
senses.note: The land east of Eden where Cain settled after leaving the presence of the LORD. Its location is unknown.

senses.name: Mehujael
senses.note: A descendant of Cain, son of Irad and father of Methushael, in the line leading to Lamech in Genesis 4.

senses.name: Tubal-cain
senses.note: Son of Lamech and Zillah in Cain's line, who made tools of bronze and iron; Naamah was his sister.

senses.name: Ham
senses.note: One of the three sons of Noah, with Shem and Japheth, and ancestor of several peoples listed in Genesis 10.

senses.name: John the Baptist
senses.note: A prophet sent by God who baptized people near the Jordan River and pointed his own disciples to Jesus. He was later imprisoned and executed by Herod Antipas; he is not the same person as John the apostle.

senses.name: John, father of Simon Peter
senses.note: The father of Simon Peter and Andrew, named when Jesus first meets Simon; nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Israel
senses.note: The people descended from Jacob, whom God renamed Israel, and the nation formed from his twelve sons' tribes. In Romans Paul wrestles with why much of Israel has not believed in Jesus as the Messiah.

senses.name: Lamech, descendant of Cain
senses.note: A descendant of Cain in the fifth generation, husband of Adah and Zillah and father of Jabal, Jubal, Tubal-Cain and Naamah. He boasts of killing a man and claims far greater vengeance than Cain.

senses.name: Lamech, father of Noah
senses.note: A descendant of Seth, son of Methuselah and father of Noah; a different man from Cain's descendant Lamech in chapter 4. He lived 777 years.

senses.name: Jacob
senses.note: Son of Isaac and grandson of Abraham, also named Israel; his twelve sons became the ancestors of Israel's tribes. Paul and the Samaritans alike look back to him as an ancestor, and his name can stand for the whole people.

senses.name: Jacob, father of Joseph
senses.note: Son of Matthan and father of Joseph, the husband of Mary, in Matthew's genealogy of Jesus; nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Mary of Bethany
senses.note: Sister of Martha and Lazarus, living in the village of Bethany near Jerusalem. She anointed Jesus with perfume and met him in grief after Lazarus died.

senses.name: Mary in Rome
senses.note: A believer in Rome whom Paul greets for her hard work on the church's behalf; nothing more is known of her.

senses.name: Isaiah
senses.note: An Israelite prophet in Jerusalem in the eighth century BC, whose prophecies make up the book of Isaiah. New Testament writers often quote him, as John the Baptist and Paul do here.

senses.name: Adam
senses.note: The first man, formed by God and placed in the garden of Eden, husband of Eve and father of Cain, Abel and Seth. The same word also means 'human being' or 'humankind'.

senses.name: Mary of Bethany
senses.note: Sister of Martha and Lazarus, living in the village of Bethany near Jerusalem, who stayed in the house while Martha went to meet Jesus.

senses.name: Mary, mother of Jesus
senses.note: A young woman engaged to Joseph of Nazareth who became pregnant through the Holy Spirit and gave birth to Jesus.

senses.name: Mahalalel
senses.note: A descendant of Seth in the line from Adam to Noah: son of Kenan and father of Jared. He lived 895 years; nothing else is told of him.

senses.name: Timothy
senses.note: Paul's close co-worker and travel companion, from Lystra, with a Jewish mother and a Greek father. He is named with Paul as co-sender of several letters, and Paul sent him to churches on his behalf.

senses.name: Jerusalem
senses.note: The chief city of Judea and site of the temple, home of the first church. Paul was taking a collection from the Gentile churches to its poor believers.

senses.name: the Jordan River
senses.note: The river running from the Sea of Galilee south to the Dead Sea, the main river of Israel. John the Baptist baptized along it, at a Bethany on its east side.

senses.name: Cana
senses.note: A village in Galilee where Jesus turned water into wine at a wedding, his first sign, and later healed an official's son. Its exact site is uncertain, probably a few miles north of Nazareth.

senses.name: Jesse
senses.note: A man of Bethlehem, grandson of Ruth and Boaz and father of King David. Isaiah's phrase 'root of Jesse' refers to a promised king from his line.

senses.name: Asia
senses.note: The Roman province in the west of what is now Turkey, with Ephesus as its leading city; not the continent.

senses.name: Sodom
senses.note: A city near the Dead Sea that God destroyed with Gomorrah for its wickedness in Abraham's time. It became a standing example of complete judgment.

senses.name: Nazareth
senses.note: A small village in the hills of Galilee where Jesus grew up. Nathanael's doubt that anything good could come from it reflects its obscurity.

senses.name: Salmon
senses.note: An ancestor of King David in Matthew's genealogy: son of Nahshon, husband of Rahab and father of Boaz.

senses.name: Josiah
senses.note: A king of Judah in the seventh century BC, remembered for his reforms of worship; he is listed among the ancestors of Jesus.

senses.name: Eliud
senses.note: An ancestor of Jesus after the exile to Babylon, listed in Matthew's genealogy as son of Achim and father of Eleazar; nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Rome
senses.note: The capital of the Roman Empire, in Italy. Paul wrote his letter to the believers there before he had visited them.

senses.name: Galatia
senses.note: A region and Roman province in central Asia Minor (modern Turkey), home to some of the scattered believers Peter addresses.

senses.name: Silvanus
senses.note: A Christian leader who helped carry or write Peter's letter; probably the same as Silas, Paul's companion on his travels in Acts.

senses.name: Beor
senses.note: The father of Balaam, the prophet hired to curse Israel in Numbers; Peter points to Balaam as an example of greed.

senses.name: Aristarchus
senses.note: A Jewish believer from Thessalonica who travelled with Paul and shared his imprisonment; he sends greetings in the letter to the Colossians.

senses.name: Luke
senses.note: A doctor and close companion of Paul who sends greetings to Colossae; traditionally the author of the Gospel of Luke and Acts.

senses.name: Archippus
senses.note: A believer at Colossae, probably connected with Philemon's household, whom Paul urges to complete the ministry he has received.

senses.name: Bethsaida
senses.note: A fishing town at the north end of the Sea of Galilee, near where the Jordan enters it; home town of Philip, Andrew and Peter.

senses.name: Caiaphas
senses.note: The Jewish high priest in Jerusalem from about AD 18 to 36, son-in-law of Annas. He urged that Jesus should die for the nation.

senses.name: Sychar
senses.note: A Samaritan town near Jacob's well, where Jesus spoke with a Samaritan woman; probably near ancient Shechem, though the exact site is uncertain.

senses.name: Iscariot
senses.note: The surname of Judas, son of Simon, the disciple who betrayed Jesus. Its meaning is uncertain; it may mean 'man from Kerioth'.

senses.name: Zerah
senses.note: A son of Judah and Tamar, twin brother of Perez, named in Matthew's genealogy of Jesus.

senses.name: Nahshon
senses.note: A leader of the tribe of Judah in Moses' time, son of Amminadab and father of Salmon; an ancestor of David and of Jesus.

senses.name: Ruth
senses.note: A Moabite woman who married Boaz of Bethlehem and became the great-grandmother of King David; her story is told in the book of Ruth.

senses.name: Jehoshaphat
senses.note: A king of Judah in the ninth century BC, son of Asa; he is listed among the ancestors of Jesus.

senses.name: Manasseh
senses.note: A king of Judah in the seventh century BC, son of Hezekiah and grandfather of Josiah, known for his long and idolatrous reign; listed among the ancestors of Jesus.

senses.name: Eliakim
senses.note: An ancestor of Jesus after the exile, listed in Matthew's genealogy as son of Abiud and father of Azor; nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Matthan
senses.note: Grandfather of Joseph, the husband of Mary, in Matthew's genealogy of Jesus; nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Euodia
senses.note: A woman in the church at Philippi who had worked alongside Paul; he urges her and Syntyche to settle their disagreement.

senses.name: Thessalonica
senses.note: A port city and capital of the Roman province of Macedonia, in northern Greece; the Philippian believers sent Paul help while he was there.

senses.name: Achaia
senses.note: The Roman province of southern Greece, with Corinth as its capital; its churches gave to the poor believers in Jerusalem.

senses.name: Aquila
senses.note: A Jewish believer and tentmaker, husband of Priscilla, who worked with Paul and risked their lives for him; a church met in their house.

senses.name: Ampliatus
senses.note: A believer in Rome whom Paul greets as dear to him in the Lord; nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Aristobulus
senses.note: A man in Rome; Paul greets the members of his household rather than him, and nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Tryphosa
senses.note: A woman in Rome, greeted with Tryphena, whom Paul commends for her work in the Lord; nothing more is known of her.

senses.name: Phlegon
senses.note: A believer in Rome whom Paul greets; nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Philologus
senses.note: A believer in Rome whom Paul greets, perhaps the husband of Julia; nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Satan
senses.note: The chief adversary of God and of his people; the name means 'adversary'. Paul promises that God will soon crush him under the believers' feet.

senses.name: Tertius
senses.note: The scribe who wrote down Paul's letter to the Romans and adds his own greeting; nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Rebecca
senses.note: Wife of Isaac and mother of the twins Jacob and Esau. Paul uses God's choice between her sons before their birth as an example.

senses.name: Pishon
senses.note: One of the four rivers flowing out of Eden, said to wind through the land of Havilah; it cannot be identified with certainty.

senses.name: Tigris
senses.note: One of the four rivers flowing out of Eden, the great river of Mesopotamia that runs east of Assyria and joins the Euphrates near the Persian Gulf.

senses.name: Enoch, son of Cain
senses.note: Cain's first son, after whom Cain named the city he was building; a different man from Enoch the descendant of Seth in chapter 5.

senses.name: Methushael
senses.note: A descendant of Cain, son of Mehujael and father of Lamech; nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Tubal-Cain
senses.note: Son of Lamech and Zillah in Cain's line, described as the first to forge tools of bronze and iron.

senses.name: Japheth
senses.note: One of Noah's three sons, with Shem and Ham, who survived the flood; later chapters trace many peoples back to him.

senses.name: the Pharisees
senses.note: A Jewish religious movement devoted to careful keeping of the law of Moses and its traditions. In John they question and oppose Jesus and join the chief priests against him; Paul says he was once a Pharisee.

senses.name: Galilee
senses.note: The northern region of the land of Israel, west of the Sea of Galilee and the Jordan, ruled in Jesus' day by Herod Antipas. Jesus grew up there and did much of his work in its towns.

senses.name: Paul
senses.note: A Jewish follower of Jesus, formerly a Pharisee who persecuted the church, who became an apostle to the Gentiles. He wrote the letters that open with his name and travelled widely founding churches.

senses.name: Enoch son of Cain
senses.note: Cain's son, after whom Cain named the city he was building; his line leads to Lamech. He is a different man from Enoch the son of Jared in Genesis 5.

senses.name: Enoch son of Jared
senses.note: A descendant of Seth through Jared and the father of Methuselah. Genesis says he walked with God and did not die in the usual way: God took him away after 365 years.

senses.name: Judea
senses.note: The southern region of the land of Israel around Jerusalem, under direct Roman rule in Jesus' day. Jesus travels between Judea and Galilee, and Paul speaks of unbelievers there opposing him.

senses.name: Simon Peter
senses.note: One of the Twelve and the brother of Andrew, a fisherman from Bethsaida. Jesus gave him the name Cephas, meaning Rock (Peter), and he became a leading apostle.

senses.name: Simon Iscariot
senses.note: The father of Judas Iscariot, the disciple who betrayed Jesus. Nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Enosh
senses.note: The son of Seth and grandson of Adam, father of Kenan. Genesis links his time with people beginning to call on the name of the LORD.

senses.name: Capernaum
senses.note: A fishing town on the north-west shore of the Sea of Galilee. Jesus made it a base for his work in Galilee; in John he heals an official's son there and teaches in its synagogue.

senses.name: Jared
senses.note: A descendant of Seth through Mahalalel and the father of Enoch, who in turn fathered Methuselah. Genesis gives him a lifespan of 962 years.

senses.name: Laodicea
senses.note: A wealthy city in the Lycus valley of Asia Minor (modern Turkey), near Colossae and Hierapolis. Paul asks the Colossians to share letters with the church there.

senses.name: Zion
senses.note: Originally the hill of David's fortress in Jerusalem, then a name for Jerusalem and its temple mount, and for God's people. The letters quote Isaiah's prophecy of a stone laid in Zion.

senses.name: Andrew
senses.note: A fisherman from Bethsaida, brother of Simon Peter and one of the Twelve. He had followed John the Baptist, and he brought his brother to Jesus.

senses.name: Samaria
senses.note: The central region of the land of Israel between Judea and Galilee, home of the Samaritans. Jesus passes through it and talks with a Samaritan woman at Jacob's well near Sychar.

senses.name: Adah
senses.note: One of the two wives of Lamech, Cain's descendant, and mother of Jabal and Jubal. Lamech addresses his boastful song to her and Zillah.

senses.name: Sarah
senses.note: The wife of Abraham, who in old age bore Isaac as God had promised. Paul cites the promise of her son, and Peter holds her up as an example to wives.

senses.name: Gomorrah
senses.note: A city near the Dead Sea, destroyed with Sodom in Genesis 19 for its wickedness. The two cities became a byword for God's judgment; the exact site is uncertain.

senses.name: the Sea of Tiberias
senses.note: Another name for the Sea of Galilee, taken from the city of Tiberias on its western shore.

senses.name: Tiberias
senses.note: A city on the western shore of the Sea of Galilee, founded by Herod Antipas around AD 20 and named after the emperor Tiberius. Boats from there came near where the crowd had been fed.

senses.name: Asa
senses.note: A king of Judah, son of Abijah and father of Jehoshaphat, remembered in Kings for removing idols. Some Greek manuscripts of Matthew spell his name Asaph.

senses.name: Jechoniah
senses.note: A king of Judah, also called Jehoiachin, who was taken into exile in Babylon. Matthew lists him in Jesus' genealogy at the turning point of the deportation.

senses.name: Epaphroditus
senses.note: A believer from Philippi who brought the church's gift to Paul in prison and helped him there. He fell seriously ill, recovered, and Paul sent him home with this letter.

senses.name: Spain
senses.note: The Roman provinces of the Iberian peninsula, at the western edge of the known world. Paul hoped to travel there after visiting Rome; whether he ever did is uncertain.

senses.name: Cappadocia
senses.note: A Roman province in central Asia Minor (modern Turkey). It is one of the regions where the believers addressed in 1 Peter lived.

senses.name: Simon Peter
senses.note: The apostle Peter, here called by the Hebrew form of his name, Simeon. He was one of the Twelve and a leader of the early church.

senses.name: Colossae
senses.note: A small city in the Lycus valley of Asia Minor (modern Turkey), near Laodicea and Hierapolis. The church there, apparently founded through Epaphras, received this letter.

senses.name: Barnabas
senses.note: A Jewish believer from Cyprus, early leader in Jerusalem and Antioch, and Paul's partner on his first mission journey. Mark is his cousin.

senses.name: Demas
senses.note: A co-worker of Paul who sends greetings with Luke. Elsewhere Paul says Demas later deserted him; nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Ephesus
senses.note: A major port city on the west coast of Asia Minor (modern Turkey), capital of the Roman province of Asia. Paul worked there for over two years; some early manuscripts lack the name in this letter.

senses.name: Thomas
senses.note: One of the Twelve, also called Didymus, meaning the Twin. He is ready to go with Jesus to Judea to die with him, and later doubts and then confesses the risen Jesus.

senses.name: Ephraim
senses.note: A town near the wilderness where Jesus withdrew with his disciples before his last Passover. It is probably the village of et-Taiyibeh north-east of Jerusalem, but the location is uncertain.

senses.name: Samaritan
senses.note: Belonging to Samaria and its people, who worshipped the God of Israel at Mount Gerizim and kept their own form of the law of Moses. Jews and Samaritans were long at odds.

senses.name: the people of Jerusalem
senses.note: Residents of Jerusalem, the city of the temple and the centre of Jewish religious life. Some of them wonder whether Jesus is the one the authorities want to kill.

senses.name: Tamar
senses.note: The daughter-in-law of Judah who bore him twin sons, Perez and Zerah (Genesis 38). She is one of the women named in Matthew's genealogy of Jesus.

senses.name: Boaz
senses.note: A landowner of Bethlehem who married Ruth the Moabite; their son Obed was David's grandfather. His mother is named as Rahab in Matthew's genealogy.

senses.name: Uriah
senses.note: A Hittite soldier in David's army whose wife Bathsheba David took; David then had Uriah killed. Matthew names Solomon's mother as Uriah's wife.

senses.name: Joram
senses.note: A king of Judah, also called Jehoram, son of Jehoshaphat. Matthew's list passes from him to Uzziah, leaving out several kings named in Kings and Chronicles.

senses.name: Amon
senses.note: A king of Judah, son of Manasseh and father of Josiah, who reigned only two years before being assassinated. Many Greek manuscripts of Matthew spell his name Amos.

senses.name: Zadok
senses.note: A descendant of Zerubbabel listed in Matthew's genealogy of Jesus after the exile. Nothing more is known of him; he is not the priest Zadok of David's time.

senses.name: Immanuel
senses.note: A name from Isaiah's prophecy meaning God is with us. Matthew applies it to Jesus, born of Mary.

senses.name: Syntyche
senses.note: A woman in the church at Philippi who had worked with Paul in spreading the gospel. Paul urges her and Euodia to agree in the Lord; nothing more is known of her.

senses.name: the emperor
senses.note: The Roman emperor, probably Nero at the time. His household included slaves and freed staff serving him, some of whom were believers sending greetings.

senses.name: Phoebe
senses.note: A woman serving the church at Cenchreae, the eastern port of Corinth, whom Paul commends to Rome; she had been a benefactor to many, and probably carried the letter.

senses.name: Epaenetus
senses.note: A believer in Rome whom Paul greets as dear to him and the first convert in the province of Asia. Nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Urbanus
senses.note: A believer in Rome whom Paul greets as a co-worker in Christ. Nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Herodion
senses.note: A believer in Rome whom Paul greets as a fellow Jew; his name may suggest a link to the household of the Herods. Nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Persis
senses.note: A woman in the church in Rome whom Paul greets as dear and as one who has worked hard in the Lord. Nothing more is known of her.

senses.name: Hermes
senses.note: A believer in Rome whom Paul greets along with others in a group. Nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Julia
senses.note: A woman in the church in Rome whom Paul greets, perhaps the wife or sister of Philologus. Nothing more is known of her.

senses.name: Lucius
senses.note: A Jewish believer with Paul in Corinth who sends greetings to Rome. He may be Lucius of Cyrene from Antioch, but this is uncertain.

senses.name: Gaius
senses.note: A believer in Corinth who hosted Paul and the whole church, probably the Gaius Paul baptized there (1 Corinthians 1:14).

senses.name: Esau
senses.note: The elder twin son of Isaac and Rebekah, brother of Jacob and ancestor of the Edomites. Paul cites the choice of Jacob over Esau to show that God's choice does not depend on human merit.

senses.name: Havilah
senses.note: A land around which the river Pishon flows, known for gold. Its location is uncertain; it is often placed in Arabia.

senses.name: Assyria
senses.note: The land on the upper Tigris in northern Mesopotamia (modern Iraq), later the centre of a great empire. Genesis places the Tigris river to its east.

senses.name: Irad
senses.note: A son of Enoch and grandson of Cain, father of Mehujael. Nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Jabal
senses.note: A son of Lamech and Adah, Cain's descendants. Genesis names him as the forerunner of those who live in tents and raise livestock.

senses.name: Naamah
senses.note: The daughter of Lamech and Zillah and sister of Tubal-cain, in Cain's line. Nothing more is known of her.

senses.name: Abraham
senses.note: The ancestor of Israel, to whom God gave promises of land and descendants. Isaac was his son, and Jews traced their descent from him; these passages debate what it means to be his true children.

senses.name: Cain
senses.note: The first son of Adam and Eve, who worked the land. He killed his brother Abel, was sent away to the land of Nod, and became the ancestor of a line that included Enoch and Lamech.

senses.name: Joseph, son of Jacob
senses.note: One of the twelve sons of Jacob, the patriarch. Jacob gave him a piece of land near Shechem, close to where the Samaritan town of Sychar later stood.

senses.name: Joseph
senses.note: The husband of Mary, the mother of Jesus, and a descendant of David. Living in Nazareth, he was known as Jesus' father; Matthew describes him as a righteous man guided by dreams.

senses.name: Simon Peter
senses.note: Simon son of John, a fisherman from Bethsaida and brother of Andrew, whom Jesus named Cephas or Peter, meaning "rock". He became a leading apostle, and two New Testament letters bear his name.

senses.name: David
senses.note: The second king of Israel, around 1000 BC, a shepherd from Bethlehem who founded a royal line. The Christ was expected to come from his family, and many psalms are attributed to him.

senses.name: Lazarus of Bethany
senses.note: The brother of Mary and Martha, living in the village of Bethany near Jerusalem. Jesus loved him, and after he died Jesus called him out of his tomb alive.

senses.name: Greeks
senses.note: People of Greek language and culture; in the New Testament the word often stands for non-Jews in general. Paul pairs "Jew and Greek" to mean all people alike.

senses.name: Abel
senses.note: The second son of Adam and Eve, a keeper of sheep and goats. The LORD accepted his offering, and his jealous brother Cain killed him; Seth was later born in his place.

senses.name: Methuselah
senses.note: The son of Enoch and father of Lamech in the line from Seth to Noah. At 969 years he is the longest-lived person recorded in the Bible.

senses.name: Nicodemus
senses.note: A Pharisee and member of the Jewish ruling council who came to Jesus at night to question him. He later spoke up for a fair hearing for Jesus and helped bury him.

senses.name: Elijah
senses.note: A prophet of the northern kingdom of Israel in the ninth century BC who opposed the worship of Baal. Malachi foretold his return before the Day of the LORD, so people asked John the Baptist if he was Elijah.

senses.name: Israelites
senses.note: Members of the people of Israel, descended from Jacob, who was also named Israel. Paul counts himself among them, and Jesus calls Nathanael a true Israelite.

senses.name: Judah
senses.note: The fourth son of Jacob and Leah, ancestor of the tribe of Judah. By Tamar he was the father of Perez and Zerah, and Matthew traces the line of David and Jesus through him.

senses.name: Judas Iscariot
senses.note: Judas son of Simon Iscariot, one of the Twelve disciples, who betrayed Jesus to the authorities.

senses.name: Zillah
senses.note: One of the two wives of Lamech, a descendant of Cain. She was the mother of Tubal-cain, the metalworker, and of a daughter, Naamah.

senses.name: Noah
senses.note: The son of Lamech and father of Shem, Ham and Japheth. God kept him and his family safe in the ark through the flood; Peter cites him as an example of rescue amid judgment.

senses.name: Epaphras
senses.note: A believer from Colossae who probably brought the gospel there and served the church. He was with Paul when Colossians was written and prayed earnestly for the Colossians.

senses.name: the pool of Siloam
senses.note: A pool in the south of Jerusalem, fed by Hezekiah's tunnel from the Gihon spring. Jesus sent a man born blind to wash there, and he came back able to see.

senses.name: Uzziah
senses.note: A king of Judah in the eighth century BC, also called Azariah, who reigned for many years. He is listed in Matthew's family line of Jesus as the father of Jotham.

senses.name: Zerubbabel
senses.note: A descendant of David and grandson of King Jehoiachin who led a group of exiles back from Babylon around 538 BC and served as governor of Judah while the temple was rebuilt.

senses.name: Benjamin
senses.note: The tribe descended from Benjamin, Jacob's youngest son; Saul, Israel's first king, came from it. Paul names it as his own tribe.

senses.name: Eve
senses.note: The first woman, wife of the man (Adam). He named her Eve because she would be the mother of all the living; she bore Cain, Abel and Seth.

senses.name: Bithynia
senses.note: A Roman province in north-west Asia Minor (modern Turkey) along the Black Sea coast. It is one of the regions where the readers of 1 Peter lived.

senses.name: Lot
senses.note: Abraham's nephew, who settled in the city of Sodom. Peter describes him as a righteous man distressed by the wickedness around him, whom God rescued when Sodom was destroyed.

senses.name: Scythians
senses.note: Nomadic peoples from the steppes north of the Black Sea, regarded by Greeks and Romans as the most uncivilized of foreigners. Paul names them to show that no background counts in Christ.

senses.name: Jesus called Justus
senses.note: A Jewish believer with Paul when he wrote Colossians, one of the few Jewish co-workers who had been a comfort to him. Nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Nympha
senses.note: A believer in or near Laodicea in whose house a church met. Paul sends her greetings; nothing more is known of her.

senses.name: Levites
senses.note: Members of the tribe of Levi who assisted the priests in the temple at Jerusalem. The Jewish leaders sent priests and Levites to question John the Baptist.

senses.name: Didymus
senses.note: A Greek nickname meaning "twin", given to Thomas, one of the Twelve disciples. Whose twin he was is not stated.

senses.name: Aenon
senses.note: A place near Salim where John the Baptist baptized because there was plenty of water. The location is uncertain; it was probably in the Jordan valley or Samaria.

senses.name: the Galileans
senses.note: The people of Galilee, the northern region of the land where Jesus grew up and did much of his work. Many had seen what he did at the festival in Jerusalem.

senses.name: Bethlehem
senses.note: A village about 9 kilometres south of Jerusalem in Judea, the hometown of David. The prophet Micah linked it with a coming ruler, so the Christ was expected to come from there.

senses.name: Hezron
senses.note: A son of Perez and grandson of Judah, listed in Matthew's family line of Jesus. Nothing more is told of him in these passages.

senses.name: Rahab
senses.note: A woman of Jericho who sheltered the Israelite spies and was spared when the city fell. Matthew lists her as the mother of Boaz in the family line of Jesus.

senses.name: Rehoboam
senses.note: Son of Solomon and king of Judah in the tenth century BC. Under him the northern tribes broke away, dividing the kingdom; he is listed in Matthew's family line of Jesus.

senses.name: Jotham
senses.note: Son of Uzziah and king of Judah in the eighth century BC. He is listed in Matthew's family line of Jesus as the father of Ahaz.

senses.name: Shealtiel
senses.note: A son of King Jechoniah born during the exile in Babylon, and father of Zerubbabel in Matthew's family line of Jesus.

senses.name: Achim
senses.note: A descendant of Zerubbabel listed in Matthew's family line of Jesus, son of Zadok and father of Eliud. Nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Philippi
senses.note: A Roman colony in Macedonia, in northern Greece, on the main road between east and west. Paul founded a church there, the first he started in Europe, and later wrote it a letter.

senses.name: Clement
senses.note: A fellow worker of Paul at Philippi who had shared in his work for the gospel. Nothing more is known of him for certain.

senses.name: Baal
senses.note: A Canaanite storm and fertility god whose worship spread in Israel in Elijah's day. God told Elijah he had kept 7,000 people who had not worshipped Baal.

senses.name: Cenchreae
senses.note: The eastern port of Corinth on the Saronic Gulf in Greece. Phoebe, whom Paul commends, served the church there.

senses.name: Andronicus
senses.note: A Jewish believer in Rome, greeted with Junia, who had been in prison with Paul and became a believer before him. They were well known among the apostles; nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Stachys
senses.note: A believer in Rome whom Paul greets as his dear friend; nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Narcissus
senses.note: The head of a household in Rome, some of whose members were believers. He himself is not greeted and was probably not a believer, or no longer living; nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Rufus
senses.note: A believer in Rome whom Paul greets along with his mother, who had cared for Paul. He may be the son of Simon of Cyrene named in Mark 15:21, but this is uncertain.

senses.name: Patrobas
senses.note: A believer in Rome whom Paul greets; nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Nereus
senses.note: A believer in Rome whom Paul greets along with his sister; nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Jason
senses.note: A Jewish believer with Paul when he wrote Romans, who sends greetings. He may be the Jason who hosted Paul in Thessalonica, but this is uncertain.

senses.name: Erastus
senses.note: The city treasurer, probably of Corinth, where Paul wrote Romans, who sends greetings. A Latin inscription found at Corinth names an official called Erastus, possibly the same man.

senses.name: Pharaoh
senses.note: The title of the king of Egypt; here the king who refused to let Israel go at the time of the exodus. Paul cites God's words to him to show God's freedom to act.

senses.name: Gihon
senses.note: The second of the four rivers flowing from Eden, said to wind through the land of Cush. Which river is meant is uncertain.

senses.name: Euphrates
senses.note: The fourth river flowing from Eden, the great river of Mesopotamia running from eastern Turkey through Syria and Iraq to the Persian Gulf.

senses.name: Mehujael
senses.note: A descendant of Cain, son of Irad and grandfather of Lamech. Nothing more is known of him.

senses.name: Jubal
senses.note: A son of Lamech and Adah, a descendant of Cain, named as the first of those who play the lyre and flute.

senses.name: Shem
senses.note: The first named of Noah's three sons, with Ham and Japheth. He is the ancestor of many peoples, including Abraham's family line.
